app.name: paperpack
app.privacy: Everything is worked out inside this browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.
app.tagline: Work out your Australian working holiday tax before you lodge it yourself.
disclaimer.body: This is a calculator, not a tax agent. It is not a registered tax agent service and nothing here is tax advice. Every figure is an estimate based on published ATO rates applied to what you typed. Check it against your own records, and if you need advice you can rely on, ask a registered tax agent.
disclaimer.confirm: I have checked these figures against my own records and understand they are an estimate.
disclaimer.effective: Rates effective {from}, last checked against the source on {checked}.
disclaimer.title: Read this before you use any number below
flag.deductions-need-written-evidence: Above 300 dollars in total work expenses you need written evidence for all of it, not just the part above 300.
flag.lodging-is-optional-but-refund-need: On working holiday wages under 45,001 dollars you are not required to lodge. But a refund only arrives if you do.
flag.medicare-entitlement-statement-may-: If you were not entitled to Medicare, an entitlement statement from Services Australia may remove this levy.
flag.medicare-exemption-claimed: The levy is left out because you said you hold an entitlement statement.
flag.nda-resident-not-calculated: You may be able to use resident rates, including the tax free threshold, because you were a resident and hold the passport of a treaty country. This calculator does not work out resident rates yet, so check with the ATO or a registered tax agent rather than using a number from here.
flag.no-tfn-withholding-is-recoverable: Tax withheld at 45 per cent because no tax file number was given is not lost. Lodging is how you get it back.
flag.resident-but-whm-rates-still-apply: Answering that you were a resident does not change your rate. Working holiday rates apply regardless of residency unless you hold the passport of one of eight treaty countries.
flag.rhca-country-medicare-likely-payabl: Your country has a reciprocal health care agreement with Australia, so you can usually enrol in Medicare, and a resident who can enrol usually pays the levy.
help.daysInAustralia: Being here more than half the year is one of the residency tests, but it is not the only one and it does not settle the question by itself.
help.grossIncome: Add up every income statement in myGov, plus any cash work. Cash counts.
help.hasMedicareEntitlementStatement: It comes from Services Australia, applications open on 1 July, and it can take up to eight weeks. Apply before you lodge, not after.
help.isAustralianTaxResident: This is your call, not ours. The ATO says most working holiday visa holders are not residents. Read the residency tests on the ATO site and answer for your own situation.
help.nationality: Nationality changes the answer for a small number of countries, because of tax treaty and health care agreements.
help.providedTfn: Without one, tax is withheld at 45 per cent. You get the excess back when you lodge.
help.taxWithheld: Also on your income statements. If an employer withheld too much, this is where the refund comes from.
help.workRelatedDeductions: Protective boots, hi vis, sunscreen for outdoor work, laundry of work clothing, tools, travel between two jobs on the same day. Not your commute, not your visa fee, not ordinary clothes.
